Subject: SLA and runbook coverage questions for upcoming pilot

Hi Kimberly / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we commit to the pilot, Procurement has flagged two things we'd like to lock down on SLA & support packaging:

- A clear definition of uptime bands by region (EU primary) and how credits are calculated for partial-day incidents.
- Rollover policy for unused retainer hours and how they apply to on-call escalation.
- Whether Redwood will integrate our runbook links into the escalation headers so our ops can triage faster (we run a hybrid on-call with CloudWave).

Can you send a concise package that combines pricing tiers + an attachable runbook integration spec? Procurement wants something we can attach to the SOW. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Simon
Simon Kent
Head of SRE, BrightMetrics

Attachment: none
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA and runbook coverage questions for upcoming pilot

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear ask.

I've attached two documents: SLA_Tier_Structure_v3.xlsx (pricing + crediting logic) and Runbook_Integration_Spec.pdf (how we surface external runbooks in alert headers and playbook links). High-level notes below:

- Uptime bands: 99.99%, 99.95%, 99.9% with pro-rata credit slabs (sheet tab: CreditCalc). For EU-region incidents we apply a regional weighting to credits if failover to another region is used.
- Partial-day incidents: credits calculated on impacted-minute basis with a minimum incident threshold of 15 minutes (this avoids micro-flap noise).
- Retainer hours: 1:1 rollover for the first 12 months, then a 50% carry-forward cap after annualization.
- Runbook integration: we can ingest a canonical HTTP(S) link or a Markdown blob. The spec includes a webhook for your CloudWave on-call system so the alert payload includes a runbook_url and a short escalation summary.

Pricing ask: for a 12-month pilot (target monthly usage ~400M tokens), we can offer a 10% starter discount on the premium response band (subject to volume true-up). I copied Marissa to confirm the discount authority and Rishi for escalation SLAs.

If you'd like, we can produce a single-page SOW appendix that folds in these tables and the integration steps (I included a draft link to a Drive file below).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Tier_Structure_v3.xlsx; Runbook_Integration_Spec.pdf

Subject: Re: SLA and runbook coverage questions for upcoming pilot

Thanks Kim — looks good. A couple of commercial clarifications from my side (thread for internal and external trace):

- The 10% starter discount is only applicable to the first 3 billing cycles and tied to the pilot commit (400M/month). We'll need a simple early-termination clause if usage falls below 50% of commit for two consecutive months.
- For escalation coverage: we can include a named on-call contact during business hours (EU CET 08:00–18:00) and an after-hours retainer for 2-hour response SLO. The retainer pricing is in the attached Excel.
- For procurement: we can accept a single SOW appendix and a short addendum with the runbook webhook details; legal wants the webhook to be one-way only (Redwood will not write back to BrightMetrics systems).

Marissa — can you confirm we have authority to extend the starter discount to 10% for this pilot and draft the SOW appendix? Rishi — please confirm the 2-hour after-hours SLO and whether we can commit to the named on-call contact language.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Ops
Redwood Inference
